question: Under the Maryland Business Occupations and Professions Article, which of these requires a real estate license?
choice_a: Regularly negotiating the purchase, sale, exchange, or lease of another person's real estate for consideration
choice_b: An owner personally selling the single home the owner lives in
choice_c: A licensed auctioneer selling real property at a public auction
choice_d: A person acting solely as a court-appointed trustee or receiver
explanation: Section 17-101 defines 'provide real estate brokerage services' to include, among other things, regularly dealing in the sale, purchase, exchange, or lease of real estate for another for consideration, which triggers the license requirement of § 17-301. Section 17-102 specifically exempts owners selling their own property, licensed auctioneers selling at public auction, and persons acting as receivers, trustees, personal representatives, or guardians.

question: Under § 17-102, an owner or lessor of real estate is exempt from Maryland real estate licensing while managing, leasing, or selling the owner's own property UNLESS:
choice_a: the property is worth more than $500,000
choice_b: the owner's or lessor's primary business is providing real estate brokerage services
choice_c: the owner does not reside in Maryland
choice_d: the property contains more than four rental units
explanation: Section 17-102(5) exempts an owner or lessor managing, leasing, or selling its own real estate, but the exemption does not apply if the owner's or lessor's primary business is providing real estate brokerage services.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-102(5)

question: Under § 17-102, a Maryland-licensed lawyer is exempt from real estate brokerage licensing only if the lawyer:
choice_a: holds any Maryland law license, regardless of how much real estate work the lawyer regularly performs
choice_b: limits real estate work to transactions under $100,000
choice_c: is not regularly engaged in the brokerage business, does not advertise as being in the brokerage business, and provides the services while representing a client in the regular practice of law
choice_d: has completed the same 60-hour salesperson pre-licensing course as other applicants
explanation: The lawyer exemption in § 17-102(2) is conditional: it applies only when the lawyer is not regularly engaged in the brokerage business, does not hold out to the public as being in that business, and provides the brokerage-type services incidentally while representing a client in the regular practice of law.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-102(2)

question: Under § 17-302, an individual may subdivide and sell unimproved property the individual owns WITHOUT a real estate license if:
choice_a: the total sale price is under $50,000
choice_b: the buyer is a family member
choice_c: the property is located outside of Maryland
choice_d: no more than 6 unimproved lots are sold by that individual in a calendar year, or the property has been owned for 10 years or more
explanation: Section 17-302 exempts an individual who sells 6 or fewer unimproved lots the individual owns in a calendar year, or who subdivides and sells unimproved property owned for 10 years or more (successive heirs may combine ownership periods to meet the 10-year threshold).
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-302

question: To transfer affiliation from one licensed broker to another under § 17-311, a real estate salesperson must:
choice_a: surrender the current license certificate and pocket card to the Commission, submit a transfer application, and provide evidence of a commitment from the new broker
choice_b: simply give verbal notice to the old broker and begin working for the new broker immediately
choice_c: wait until the next 2-year renewal cycle before changing brokers
choice_d: retake and pass the salesperson licensing examination
explanation: Section 17-311(c) requires the salesperson or associate broker to surrender the license certificate and pocket card, submit a transfer application, submit acknowledgment (or a statement) that the current affiliation is terminated, provide evidence of a commitment from the new broker, and pay the transfer fee before the Commission issues a new license.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-311

question: Under § 17-312, a real estate salesperson may exchange the salesperson license directly for a broker license WITHOUT re-satisfying the § 17-305 education and experience requirements only if the salesperson:
choice_a: has simply worked as a salesperson for at least 3 years, regardless of license history
choice_b: previously held an associate real estate broker or real estate broker license and has held a license continuously since first being licensed at that level
choice_c: has completed the current cycle's 15 hours of continuing education
choice_d: has a broker willing to sponsor the exchange
explanation: Section 17-312(b) allows a salesperson to exchange directly for a broker license without redoing § 17-305's education/experience requirements only if the salesperson previously held an associate broker or broker license and has held a license continuously since first being licensed at that level.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-312(b)

question: According to Maryland Real Estate Commission (MREC) guidance, how does a licensee change license status between active and inactive?
choice_a: Only by submitting a notarized paper form in person at the Commission's office
choice_b: Only during the licensee's renewal window
choice_c: Electronically, by using the Commission's online 'Change Your Information or Status' feature and selecting inactive/reactivate
choice_d: Only through an attorney retained by the licensee
explanation: MREC's licensing FAQ page states that a licensee may change status online through the electronic licensing system's 'Change Your Information or Status' feature, choosing inactive/reactivate as needed.
source_note: Maryland Real Estate Commission Licensing FAQs, dllr.state.md.us/license/mrec/mreclicfaqs.shtml

question: Under § 17-320(e), when a broker terminates the affiliation of a salesperson or associate broker, the broker must:
choice_a: simply stop paying commissions to the individual
choice_b: wait for the Commission to initiate the termination process
choice_c: report the termination only at the next license renewal
choice_d: notify the individual by mail, submit written notice to the Commission, and return the individual's license certificate to the Commission
explanation: Section 17-320(e) requires a broker, on termination of an affiliation, to immediately notify the agent or associate broker by mail, submit written notice to the Commission, and return the license certificate to the Commission.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-320(e)

question: Under § 17-314(c), a Maryland real estate license, once renewed, is issued for an additional term of:
choice_a: 2 years
choice_b: 1 year
choice_c: 3 years
choice_d: 4 years
explanation: Section 17-314(c)(1) provides that a licensee may renew a license for an additional 2-year term upon meeting the statutory renewal conditions.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-314(c)(1)

question: Under § 17-314(c)(1)(iv), a licensee's required continuing education for renewal must be completed:
choice_a: on the exact date the license expires
choice_b: not later than 30 days before the license expires
choice_c: within 30 days after the renewal application is filed
choice_d: at any point during the 2-year term, with no fixed deadline
explanation: Section 17-314(c)(1)(iv) requires that, not later than 30 days before the license expires, the licensee has complied with the continuing education requirements of § 17-315. MREC guidance notes that missing this deadline can trigger a reinstatement fee.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-314(c)(1)(iv)

question: Under § 17-314(e), the Commission will reinstate an expired Maryland real estate license if the former licensee applies for reinstatement within:
choice_a: 6 months after expiration
choice_b: 1 year after expiration
choice_c: 3 years after the license expired, and meets character, continuing education, and fee requirements
choice_d: 5 years after expiration
explanation: Section 17-314(e) requires the Commission to reinstate an expired license if the applicant applies within 3 years after expiration, meets good character and reputation requirements, complies with applicable continuing education for the unlicensed period, and pays the reinstatement fee.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-314(e)

question: Under § 17-314(b), the Commission mails or electronically transmits a license renewal notice to:
choice_a: the licensee's home address only, regardless of affiliation
choice_b: the Commission's own headquarters for internal processing
choice_c: whichever address appears on the licensee's driver's license
choice_d: the principal office of the licensee's broker (the licensee's own office if a broker, or the sponsoring broker's office if an associate broker or salesperson)
explanation: Section 17-314(b)(2) directs renewal materials to the principal office of the real estate broker: the broker's own principal office if the licensee is a broker, or the office of the broker with whom an associate broker or salesperson is affiliated.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-314(b)(2)

question: Under § 17-314(c)(1)(vi), which additional renewal item applies specifically to a real estate broker (and not to a salesperson)?
choice_a: Submission of a credit report from a Commission-approved agency, or payment of a credit report fee
choice_b: An FBI criminal background check
choice_c: Proof of errors-and-omissions insurance
choice_d: A letter of recommendation from another broker
explanation: Section 17-314(c)(1)(vi) requires a real estate broker renewing a license to submit a credit report from a Commission-approved agency, or pay a fee for the actual cost of a credit report.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-314(c)(1)(vi)

question: Under § 17-315, how many clock hours of continuing education must a Maryland real estate licensee complete during each 2-year renewal term?
choice_a: 8 clock hours
choice_b: 15 clock hours
choice_c: 30 clock hours
choice_d: 45 clock hours
explanation: Section 17-315 requires a licensee to complete at least 15 clock hours of continuing education instruction during the preceding 2-year license term as a condition of renewal.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-315

question: Under § 17-315, brokers, branch managers, and team leaders must include, within their 15 hours of continuing education, a course of at least:
choice_a: 8 hours of property management
choice_b: 10 hours of appraisal principles
choice_c: 1.5 clock hours addressing the requirements of broker supervision
choice_d: There is no supervision-specific course requirement for brokers
explanation: Section 17-315 specifically requires brokers and designated managers to include at least a 1.5 clock hour course covering the requirements of broker supervision as part of their continuing education.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-315; MREC continuing education requirements chart, dllr.state.md.us/license/mrec/mreceducreq.shtml

question: Which continuing education topics are mandatory for renewal (and, per MREC guidance, may not be substituted with out-of-state coursework) for brokers, branch managers, and team leaders?
choice_a: Property management, appraisal, home inspection, and mortgage lending
choice_b: Only an ethics course
choice_c: Only fair housing and legal update courses
choice_d: Legal and legislative update (3 hrs), fair housing (2 hrs), ethics (3 hrs), and principles of brokerage relationships and disclosure (3 hrs)
explanation: Section 17-315 sets minimum hours for legal/legislative update, fair housing, ethics, and brokerage relationships/disclosure, and MREC's continuing education chart identifies these as mandatory topics for brokers, branch managers, and team leaders that may not be substituted with out-of-state education.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-315; MREC continuing education requirements chart, dllr.state.md.us/license/mrec/mreceducreq.shtml

question: Per current Maryland Real Estate Commission guidance (effective October 1, 2024), continuing education for renewal generally must be completed:
choice_a: at least 30 days before the renewal application is submitted, to avoid triggering a reinstatement fee
choice_b: only during the final week before the license expires
choice_c: only during the first year of the 2-year license term
choice_d: at any time, since there is no deadline connected to renewal
explanation: MREC guidance, consistent with § 17-314(c)(1)(iv), states that CE courses must be completed at least 30 days prior to the license renewal date to avoid a reinstatement fee, effective October 1, 2024.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-314(c)(1)(iv); MREC continuing education page, dllr.state.md.us/license/mrec/mreceduc.shtml

question: Under § 17-101's definitions, a Maryland 'real estate broker' is legally defined as:
choice_a: a corporation registered with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to conduct real estate business
choice_b: an individual who provides real estate brokerage services
choice_c: any partnership in which a majority of the partners hold real estate licenses
choice_d: a limited liability company organized for the purpose of conducting real estate transactions
explanation: Section 17-101 defines 'real estate broker' as an individual who provides real estate brokerage services; the definitions section contains no separate licensing category for corporations, partnerships, or LLCs.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-101

question: Because Maryland law defines 'real estate broker' as an individual, a corporation or partnership that wants to operate a real estate brokerage business in Maryland must:
choice_a: obtain a single corporate broker license that covers all of its agents collectively
choice_b: ensure at least 51% of its shares are owned by a licensed broker in place of any individual licensing requirement
choice_c: conduct its brokerage activities through one or more individuals who personally hold real estate broker licenses, since the entity itself cannot be licensed as a broker
choice_d: simply register the entity's name with the Commission; no individual license is required
explanation: Because §§ 17-101 and 17-301 define and license only individuals as real estate brokers, a business entity cannot itself hold a broker license; it must operate through individually licensed brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. §§ 17-101, 17-301(a)

question: Maryland's real estate licensing statute does not set a minimum percentage of stock or partnership ownership that a licensed broker must hold in a real estate business. This is because:
choice_a: the Commission negotiates an ownership percentage separately with each brokerage
choice_b: state law fixes a required 50% broker-ownership threshold instead
choice_c: ownership percentage in real estate firms is regulated by the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation, not Title 17
choice_d: the broker license attaches to the individual who provides brokerage services, not to any ownership share in the business entity
explanation: Since Title 17 licenses only individuals (§ 17-101, § 17-301), and not business entities, there is no statutory ownership-percentage threshold; licensure depends on the individual providing brokerage services, regardless of how the underlying business is owned.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. §§ 17-101, 17-301(a)

question: Under § 17-317, a licensed real estate broker must display the broker's license certificate:
choice_a: at all times, in a conspicuous place in the broker's principal office
choice_b: only when a client specifically asks to see it
choice_c: in a locked file accessible only to the broker
choice_d: only at the Commission's office in Baltimore
explanation: Section 17-317 requires a licensed real estate broker to display the license certificate at all times in a conspicuous place in the broker's principal office, and to display affiliated licensees' certificates in the appropriate office as well.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-317

question: Under § 17-313(i), if a licensed real estate broker operates more than one real estate brokerage business, the broker must:
choice_a: obtain one license that simply lists all business locations
choice_b: obtain a separate real estate broker license for each brokerage operated
choice_c: register any additional locations with the county government only
choice_d: license only the main office; branch locations are exempt from licensing
explanation: Section 17-313(i) requires a licensed real estate broker to obtain a real estate broker license for each real estate brokerage operated by that broker.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-313(i)

question: Under § 17-320(c)-(d), the supervisory duties of a branch office manager over agents working out of that branch:
choice_a: fully substitute for and eliminate the broker's own supervisory obligation for that branch
choice_b: apply only when the broker is physically unavailable
choice_c: supplement, but do not replace, the licensed broker's own duty to exercise reasonable and adequate supervision
choice_d: are a matter of company policy only, with no basis in Maryland statute
explanation: Section 17-320(c) imposes a general duty of reasonable and adequate supervision on the broker, and § 17-320(d) makes clear that branch manager oversight supplements, rather than replaces, that broker-level supervisory duty.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-320(c)-(d)

question: Under § 17-305, to qualify for a Maryland real estate broker's license, an applicant must generally complete a Commission-approved broker pre-licensing course of how many classroom hours?
choice_a: 60 hours
choice_b: 90 hours
choice_c: 180 hours
choice_d: 135 hours
explanation: Section 17-305 requires completion of a Commission-approved real estate course as part of broker qualification; the Maryland Real Estate Commission's broker licensing FAQ specifies this course must be a 135-clock-hour broker pre-licensing course from an approved education provider.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-305(d); Maryland Real Estate Commission broker licensing FAQ, dllr.state.md.us/license/mrec/mreclicfaqs.shtml

question: Under § 17-305, an applicant for a Maryland real estate broker's license must have held an active, regular, and lawful license providing real estate brokerage services (as a salesperson or associate broker) for at least:
choice_a: 3 consecutive years immediately before applying
choice_b: 1 year
choice_c: 2 years
choice_d: 5 years
explanation: Section 17-305(d)(1) requires at least 3 years of active, regular, and lawful real estate brokerage practice as a licensed salesperson (or associate broker) before qualifying for a broker license; MREC's FAQ confirms this as 3 consecutive years immediately prior to applying.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-305(d)(1); Maryland Real Estate Commission broker licensing FAQ, dllr.state.md.us/license/mrec/mreclicfaqs.shtml

question: Under § 17-305(d)(2), which type of applicant may have the standard broker pre-licensing education and experience requirements waived?
choice_a: A licensed salesperson with 5 years of experience
choice_b: A lawyer authorized to practice law in Maryland
choice_c: A licensed home inspector
choice_d: A licensed auctioneer
explanation: Section 17-305(d)(2) provides that a lawyer qualified to practice law in Maryland may have the standard broker education and experience requirements waived.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-305(d)(2)

question: Under §§ 17-303 and 17-305, both the salesperson and broker pre-licensing courses in Maryland must each include a separate ethics component of:
choice_a: 1 clock hour
choice_b: 6 clock hours
choice_c: 3 clock hours
choice_d: There is no separate ethics component; it is folded into the general course
explanation: Both § 17-303(d) (salesperson) and § 17-305(d)(1) (broker) require completion of a separate 3 clock hour course in real estate ethics, in addition to the general pre-licensing coursework.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. §§ 17-303(d), 17-305(d)(1)

question: Under § 17-319, if a licensed Maryland real estate broker dies or becomes permanently disabled, an adult family member may operate the brokerage to close it out for a maximum of:
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 1 year
choice_c: 2 years
choice_d: 6 months
explanation: Section 17-319(b) allows an adult family member of a deceased or disabled broker to operate the business for up to 6 months to close and terminate it, subject to providing required documentation to the Commission.
source_note: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 17-319(b)
